reason: Same software (Zen Browser) across sources with genuinely different naming — Flathub's short display name "Zen" vs AUR's "zen-browser" family — that no safe name pattern can bridge on its own; zen alone is also now GENERIC_NAME_BLOCKLIST-ed (see group.ts) since it collides with an unrelated AUR C-language tool. User-reported false-negative merge.

Same software (GNOME Boxes) across sources with genuinely different naming — Flathub's short display name "Boxes" doesn't normalize-match "gnome-boxes", the name every native distro package (and Snap) uses instead. Found investigating the compat-warnings feature: "boxes" alone is also now GENERIC_NAME_BLOCKLIST-ed (see group.ts) since it was wrongly false-merging with an unrelated ASCII-art text tool of the same name.

Same software (LibreOffice) — Arch's own release-channel naming (libreoffice-fresh, and its maintenance-branch twin libreoffice-still) never exact-matches any other source's bare "libreoffice" appId/name, so both stay stray standalone entries despite being kept (see filter-keep.json). Found during an ultra-style review pass that also uncovered the keep-list coverage gap for LibreOffice/LibreCAD across apk-alpine/ebuild-gentoo/eopkg-solus/nix-nixpkgs/snap-snapcraft/xbps-void.

Same software (Beeper) as the new official beeper.com AppImage entry — AUR's beeper-bin/beeper-nightly-bin already auto-merge with it via tier2's normalized-name match (both normalize to "beeper"), but beeper-v4-bin's "v4" isn't a recognized AUR channel-word/variant-suffix component (see group.ts's AUR_CHANNEL_WORD/AUR_VARIANT_SUFFIX), so it strips down to "beeper-v4" instead and stays a stray. User-reported — needed for baxyz's influencer recommendations page.

Same software (Node.js) — Snap's official "Node.js Runtime" snap is named "node", not "nodejs" like every other source's bare-appId package (Alpine/Arch/Debian/Ubuntu/Gentoo/Nixpkgs/Slackware/Solus/Void, already unioned into one group via tier1's exact appId match), so it stays a stray standalone entry. User-reported. Fedora's nodejs20/22/24/26 deliberately NOT included here — real, separately-installable parallel major-version-stream packages (Fedora Modularity convention, no single unversioned "nodejs" package exists there), not duplicate names for the same install target.

Same software (the real VICE Commodore 8-bit emulator) across sources: Flathub's own net.sf.VICE listing, Debian's bare "vice" (already tier1-merged with Ubuntu/Arch/Nix/RPM Fusion/Void/Solus via their own identical bare appId, no force needed for those), Gentoo's category-qualified app-emulation/vice, and AUR's rolling-release vice-svn build. All of these normalize to the same bare "vice" name Flathub's OTHER, unrelated "Vice" (io.github.mmp.Vice, an air traffic control simulator) also shares — see config/match-deny.json's io.github.mmp.Vice entries, which is why tier2's normalized-name bridge is deliberately blocked for this whole family and each real member needs reattaching here instead. Picking net.sf.VICE as the force destination (rather than a distro package) gives the real emulator a clean Flathub-appId id instead of an arbitrary source:appId fallback. Found live surfaced while working the games "To Classify" bucket (2026-09-02).

Same software (the Elm programming-language compiler) across sources -- AUR's elm-git is its rolling-release build, Nixpkgs' elmPackages.elm the same compiler under nixpkgs' own attribute-path convention. The new config/match-deny.json entries separating this cluster from AUR's unrelated bare "elm" (The Elm Mail System, a real terminal mail client sharing the identical normalized name) also block these two from ever reaching each other or the compiler's own AUR binary build on their own, since tier2's "elm" representative was that mail client. Found live investigating the apps "To Classify" bucket (2026-09-02) while adding the elm-* category rule.

Same software (Convoy, the roguelike vehicle-combat game) across GOG and Lutris. The existing match-deny.json entries correctly keep AUR's unrelated bare "convoy" (a Docker volume plugin) separate from both, but the deny-via-representative interaction in group.ts's tier2 left GOG's own listing and Lutris's two installer slugs (convoy-gog / convoy-humble-bundle) split into three standalone groups too -- each Lutris side stayed "To Classify" while GOG's side carried the real genre. Found live reviewing the "24 duplicate group names" matching card (2026-09-04).

The existing match-deny.json entries correctly keep AUR's unrelated deadbolt-bin (a file-encryption tool) separate, but left GOG's own listing and Lutris's deadbolt-gog installer slug split -- Lutris's side stayed "To Classify" while GOG's side carried the real Action genre. Found live reviewing the "24 duplicate group names" matching card (2026-09-04).

Same software (the ASCII-art "boxes" text-drawing tool, boxes.thomasjensen.com) packaged under the same bare "boxes" name across AUR/Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora/Nixpkgs/Gentoo. The GENERIC_NAME_BLOCKLIST entry for "boxes" (added to stop GNOME Boxes from false-merging with this unrelated tool -- see group.ts) also prevented these six identical packages from merging with each other, leaving Fedora/Nixpkgs stranded as separate "To Classify" groups. GNOME Boxes itself is packaged as "gnome-boxes" in every native source, so re-merging the bare-"boxes" cluster cannot pull it in. Found live reviewing the "24 duplicate group names" matching card (2026-09-04).

Same software (the FUSE filesystem interface / reference implementation) packaged under the same bare "fuse" name across Debian/Ubuntu/Fedora/Nixpkgs/openSUSE/Alpine/Void/Solus and Gentoo's sys-fs/fuse. The GENERIC_NAME_BLOCKLIST entry for "fuse" (added because the bare word also names the ZX Spectrum emulator -- see group.ts) also prevented these nine identical filesystem packages from merging with each other, leaving Fedora/Nixpkgs/Alpine/Void stranded as separate "To Classify" groups. The emulator is packaged as flatpak's net.sourceforge.fuse_emulator.Fuse and Gentoo's app-emulation/fuse -- neither is listed here, so it stays its own separate group. Found live reviewing the "24 duplicate group names" matching card (2026-09-04).
